priority_and_shaping_requirements: Per-route priority lanes: high (realtime scoring), medium (personalization), low (batch embeddings).
Hard per-route quotas: ability to reserve min RPS for high lane and burstable capacity for medium lane.
Tenant isolation: CPU/GPU tenant pinning and memory/KV cache partitioning to avoid cross-tenant cache eviction.
Noisy-neighbor controls: request rate limiting, backpressure signals, automatic downscaling of noisy processes and pre-emptible lower-priority queues.
Observability: token-level latency breakdown, per-route queue depth, and per-tenant GPU utilization dashboards.
performance_targets: Baseline reserved capacity target: 2k RPS for high-priority path (avg payload 40 tokens) sustained; burst to 6k for 30s windows.
Latency SLOs: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms on reserved baseline; tail guarantees must hold during steady state.
Throughput planning: initial reserved pool equivalent to 8 x A100 (or 16 x A10s) with autoscaling headroom of +50% as burst buffer.
Fallback policy: automatic routing to warmed secondary model variant (quantized) with explicit quality delta tracked in evals.
sla_and_contract_notes: Legal: requires uptime SLA + latency SLOs tied to credits; escalation matrix with 1-hour P1 response and 4-hour mitigation window.
Request to include explicit network isolation clause and data return/secure-wipe on termination.
